newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up at 72.4 bln levs Aug 31.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up at 72.4 bln levs Aug 31.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose 2.7 billion levs in the second half of August to 72.4 billion levs, or 89.7 percent of the revised 1996 deficit target, according to finance ministry figures.
Between August 17-30, expenditures gained 12.7 billion levs to 235.3 billion levs, or 76.3 percent of the total expenditures planned for the whole year in the revised budget.
Revenue grew by 10 billion levs to 162.9 billion levs, or 65.1 percent of the target.
On July 30, parliament revised the country's 1996 budget in a move to meet higher foreign and domestic debt payments and keep the structural reform on track.

In the revised budget, revenue was set at 358.2 billion levs and spending at 438.9 billion levs. The deficit was assumed at 4.9 percent of gross domestic product or 80.7 billion levs, up from the original 58.3 billion levs.

Under the revised 1996 budget, Bulgaria will also allocate 52.6 percent, or 321 billion levs, of expenditures planned for the year to cover interest payments on foreign and domestic debt. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 84561
